subject: Peru
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about Lake Titicaca. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). The lake has no outline in the pinned map data, so it is a labelled approximate point on the Peru–Bolivia border. "Highest navigable lake" is how the article puts it: "often called", so the episode keeps that hedge.

claims.text: Lake Titicaca is a large lake in the Andes mountains on the border of Bolivia and Peru.
It is often called the highest navigable lake in the world.
Titicaca is the largest lake in South America, both in terms of the volume of water and surface area.
The western part of the lake lies within the Puno Region of Peru, and the eastern side is located in the Bolivian La Paz Department.
It is often listed as a freshwater lake, though its waters are slightly brackish.
